Offline Computing
docs.text:
Most modern applications assume constant internet access.

This assumption is fragile.

Good software should work even when the network fails.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Git is a great example of offline-first software.

docs.title: TCP Hole Punching
docs.text: TCP hole punching is a technique used to establish direct connections between peers behind NAT.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Two peers behind NAT cannot directly connect.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Both peers connect to a rendezvous server
  2. The server exchanges their addresses
  3. Both attempt simultaneous connections

This allows NAT mappings to open on both sides.
